territorial_scope.description: Directs United States federal executive agencies and the Task Force; applies nationally.

evidence.quote: There is hereby established the White House Task Force on Artificial Intelligence Education (Task Force).

summary.short: Executive order directing federal agencies to promote AI literacy through education and workforce programs. Establishes a White House AI Education Task Force, a Presidential AI Challenge, K-12 AI resources, educator training priorities and AI-related Registered Apprenticeships, with 90-, 120- and 180-day deadlines from the order's date.
summary.long: Directs federal agencies to promote AI literacy and an AI-ready workforce through education programs. Establishes the White House Task Force on AI Education, chaired by the OSTP Director, to coordinate federal efforts (Sec. 4). Within 90 days the Task Force plans a Presidential AI Challenge, to be held within 12 months of the plan's submission (Sec. 5). Agencies seek public-private partnerships for K-12 AI resources, prioritize related funding where consistent with law, and within 180 days of the first partnership announcement aim to have resources ready (Sec. 6). Within 120 days the Education Secretary is to prioritize AI in teacher-training grants and NSF is to prioritize AI-in-education research (Sec. 7). Within 120 days the Labor Secretary is to increase AI-related Registered Apprenticeships, set goals and performance targets, and prioritize grants for high school AI courses (Sec. 8). The order is subject to applicable law and appropriations and creates no enforceable rights (Sec. 9).

relations.note: Sec. 3 defines 'artificial intelligence' or 'AI' by reference to this provision of the U.S. Code; the definition is taken from that provision rather than restated.

evidence.quote: has the meaning set forth in 15 U.S.C. 9401(3)

notes: The provided text has no statement of enabling legal authority, no signature date and no order number, so no legal_basis relation is coded. Sec. 9(c) states the order creates no enforceable rights.

thresholds.note: The order contains no numeric cutoffs that change legal treatment. Its only numbers are procedural time limits (e.g., Sec. 5(a) 90 days, 12 months; Sec. 6(a)(ii) 180 days; Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 120 days), which are deadlines for events, not thresholds. Section 3 defines AI by reference to 15 U.S.C. 9401(3), with no numeric scope test.
